_doc: Every render script (tools/sprites/render_sprites.py, render_characters.py, render_anakin.py, render_city.py, render_building.py) reads its settings from this file; command-line options only pick the asset, a preview or a forced re-render. See CLAUDE.md for the rules.

device._doc: auto: Cycles on the GPU when Blender finds one (OptiX, CUDA, HIP, oneAPI, Metal), else the CPU; cpu / gpu force it. This container has no GPU: 4 CPU cores, EEVEE only as a slow software renderer.

character._doc: Sprite sheets of characters (one Blender run per character, every direction of a frame in one tiled render, colour + shadow (+ optional passes) out of that one render).
character._engine_doc: cycles everywhere: EEVEE has no shadow catcher, so its shadow needs a second render (against the one-render rule), and without a GPU it is a slow software renderer (27.5 s a frame vs 4.7 s; with hair over 20 min). On a GPU machine eevee can be tried here; the script then renders the shadow separately.
character._denoiser_doc: none: measured — OIDN costs 1.2 s of a 4 s frame and makes no visible difference after the 2x downscale (mean |diff| < 0.25/255 at 128 px). OPENIMAGEDENOISE to turn it back on.
character._passes_doc: color and shadow are what the game draws; normal (camera space, RGB = n·0.5+0.5) lights the characters by transient lights (src/gfx/relight.js: sabers, bolts, clashes, explosions). depth (8 bit, ±depth_range units round the feet) comes out of the same render when listed; the game does not use it yet. Each extra pass adds a sheet per character.
character._shadow_doc: the shadow is the Shadow Catcher pass of the same render, on a disc under each direction (shadow_patch_radius units); the dim sky fills it a little, shadow_gain brings it back to the darkness of the old separate key-light-only shadow render
character._mirror_doc: Mirror: render only the directions that are not a left-right mirror of another and flip them for the rest (about half the renders). It swaps the model's sides, so the saber hand changes: only for sprites listed in mirror_sprites (symmetric, nothing held in one hand).

sprites._doc: Sprites modelled in Blender (tools/sprites/build_anakin.py outfits); the other characters' directions come from src/gfx/specs.js.

building._doc: City assets baked once (body / neon / reflection layers): Cycles, more samples on a GPU.

preview._doc: --preview: a quick look at a new feature instead of a full render — one direction (front: facing the camera), two frames of each animation, written to tools/sprites/out/preview.

parallel._doc: Characters rendered side by side. CPU: two keep 4 cores busier than one (a render's fixed costs are partly single-threaded). GPU: two share one GPU (one syncs the scene while the other renders).

estimate._doc: Before rendering, the scripts print the number of images and the expected time (seconds per frame from tools/sprites/out/render_times.json, measured on earlier runs, else these defaults per tiled frame); above ask_minutes they stop unless run with --yes.
